Mon Nov 9markets

Taiex jumps 4.94% in its second-largest daily point gain after Taiwan authorizes stabilization fund

Taiwan's Taiex rose 1,960.06 points, or 4.94%, to 41,661.70 on Monday, its second-largest single-day point gain, after the National Financial Stabilization Fund's management committee authorized market intervention on Friday, Focus Taiwan reported.

Mon Nov 9regulation

South Korea fines Baemin and Coupang a combined 631.9 billion won over price-matching demands on restaurants

South Korea's Fair Trade Commission said Monday it will impose provisional fines of 331.1 billion won on Woowa Brothers, operator of delivery app Baemin, and 300.8 billion won on Coupang, which runs Coupang Eats, for requiring restaurants to offer terms no less favorable than on rival apps, Yonhap and the Korea Herald reported.

Mon Nov 9business

Mitsui Chemicals to buy chip materials maker JSR for 1.84 trillion yen with Development Bank of Japan

Mitsui Chemicals said Monday it will acquire semiconductor materials maker JSR from state-backed Japan Investment Corp. (JIC) for 1.84 trillion yen ($11.61 billion), with the Development Bank of Japan (DBJ) investing 200 billion yen, according to a company filing and Reuters.

Mon Nov 9diplomacy

Japan and Vietnam sign 10 deals on energy, technology and security as To Lam visits Tokyo

Japan and Vietnam announced 10 agreements and pledged to raise bilateral trade to as much as $100 billion by 2030 as Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi met Vietnamese President and Communist Party General Secretary To Lam in Tokyo on Monday, Bloomberg reported in the Japan Times.

Mon Nov 9security

Japanese retailer Nitori says up to 37.62 million customer records may have leaked after unauthorized access

Japanese home furnishings retailer Nitori Holdings said Monday that up to 37.62 million customer records, including email and home addresses, may have leaked through unauthorized access, though login passwords and credit card details were not compromised, Kyodo and Nikkei reported.

Sun Nov 8disaster

Magnitude 5.7 quake in central Japan injures more than 20

A magnitude 5.7 earthquake struck western Shizuoka Prefecture at 1:04 a.m. Sunday, injuring more than 20 people in Aichi and Shizuoka, according to the Japan Meteorological Agency and Kyodo, as reported by AP and Al Jazeera.

Sun Nov 8elections

Taiwan court detains Taiwan People's Communist Party chief in election-funding probe

A Taiwan court ordered Lin Te-wang, chairman of the small Taiwan People's Communist Party, detained incommunicado after prosecutors alleged he took instructions and funding from China's Communist Party to run in a local election, Focus Taiwan and the Taipei Times reported.

Sun Nov 8policy

Second batch of three F-16V Block 70 jets arrives in Taiwan

Three F-16V Block 70 fighters bought from the United States landed at Chihhang Air Base in Taitung on Sunday, Taiwan's air force said, according to Focus Taiwan and the Taipei Times.

Sat Nov 7markets

Taiwan activates NT$500 billion stabilization fund after Taiex rout

Taiwan's National Financial Stabilization Fund on Friday authorized market intervention after the Taiex fell 1,873.08 points, or 4.51%, to 39,701.64, the Ministry of Finance and Focus Taiwan reported.

Sat Nov 7diplomacy

Putin places more Japan Tobacco assets in Russia under local control

Russian President Vladimir Putin on Friday put additional Japan Tobacco units in Russia under temporary local management, a day after a decree covering four JT International subsidiaries.

Fri Nov 6markets

Nikkei, KOSPI and Taiex plunge as fears of US curbs on AI data centers hit Asian chip stocks

Japan's Nikkei 225 fell 5.96% to 57,434.77, South Korea's KOSPI dropped 6.02% to 5,059.69 and Taiwan's Taiex lost 4.51% to 39,701.64 on Friday, as worries that a Democratic-led US Congress could slow AI data-center building hit technology shares, the Japan Times, Yonhap and Focus Taiwan reported.

Fri Nov 6courts

Malaysia's attorney general halts Najib's move to house arrest after Umno pays his 50 million ringgit fine

Malaysia's attorney general on Friday temporarily blocked former prime minister Najib Razak's transfer from prison to house arrest, saying more legal clarification was needed, after his party Umno paid the 50 million ringgit fine required under a royal pardon, AP and Malay Mail reported.

Fri Nov 6courts

Macao court jails former lawmaker Au Kam San for 12.5 years in first national security case

A Macao court on Friday sentenced former pro-democracy lawmaker Au Kam San, 69, to 12.5 years in prison in the city's first national security case, convicting him of subverting state power, establishing links with outside groups to endanger national security and breach of secrecy, RTHK and AP reported.

Fri Nov 6policy

Japan's lower house passes bill to cut the consumption tax on food to 1% for two years

Japan's House of Representatives on Friday passed a bill to cut the consumption tax on food from 8% to 1% for two years from April 2027 and to create income-linked cash payments, sending it to the upper house, where the ruling coalition lacks a majority, NHK, Kyodo and Jiji Press reported.

Fri Nov 6policy

Singapore and Malaysia to raise cross-border taxi quota to 500 each from Nov. 16

Singapore and Malaysia will raise the quota of licensed cross-border taxis from 300 to 500 per country from Nov. 16 and license two more ride-hail operators, the two transport ministries said in a joint statement on Friday.

Thu Nov 5courts

Hong Kong court sentences activist Joshua Wong to 10 years for foreign collusion

Hong Kong's High Court on Thursday sentenced pro-democracy activist Joshua Wong to 10 years in prison after he pleaded guilty to conspiring to collude with foreign forces under the national security law, RTHK and the AP reported.

Thu Nov 5markets

Seoul stocks plunge 5.28% and Taipei drops 3.2% as AI worries hit chipmakers after US midterms

South Korea's KOSPI fell 300 points, or 5.28%, to close at 5,383.80 on Thursday, and Taiwan's Taiex dropped 3.2% to 41,574.72, as worries that the U.S. midterm results could slow AI investment hit technology shares, Yonhap and Focus Taiwan reported.

Thu Nov 5crypto

South Korea to seek a two-year delay in its crypto gains tax, pushing it to 2029

South Korea will ask the National Assembly to postpone a tax on cryptocurrency gains from 2027 to 2029, Finance Minister Lee Hyoung-il said on Thursday, in what would be the fourth delay since the tax was legislated in 2020.

Thu Nov 5security

NTT Docomo says a hack leaked data on up to about 300,000 customers

NTT Docomo said on Thursday that unauthorized access to its online shop and My docomo portal leaked some customer information, affecting up to about 300,000 records, including names, addresses, dates of birth and phone numbers.

Thu Nov 5policy

South Korea plans to expand its anti-piracy naval mission toward the Strait of Hormuz

South Korea plans to extend its Cheonghae anti-piracy unit's operating area from the Gulf of Aden to waters south of Oman and add a P-8A maritime patrol aircraft and mine-clearing assets, officials said on Thursday, pending National Assembly approval.

Mon Nov 2economy

South Korea's exports jump 93.7% to a record $115.3 billion in October on chip demand

South Korea's exports rose 93.7% from a year earlier to a record $115.3 billion in October, driven by a 259% jump in semiconductor shipments, the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources said on Sunday.

Mon Nov 2disaster

Japan launches a national agency to lead disaster preparedness and response

Japan's government on Monday launched the National Disaster Management Agency, a new body headed by Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi to coordinate the country's response to disasters, according to AP, Kyodo News and NHK.

Mon Nov 2diplomacy

Taiwan says China's handling of its APEC summit invitation broke with established practice

Taiwan's Foreign Minister Lin Chia-lung on Monday called on China, this year's APEC host, to follow established practice in formally inviting Taiwan to the Nov. 18-19 leaders' summit in Shenzhen, according to Focus Taiwan and the Taipei Times.

Mon Nov 2economy

Johor-Singapore economic zone has drawn 88.83 billion ringgit in approved investments, ministers say

The Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone recorded 88.83 billion ringgit (S$28.1 billion) in approved investments from January 2025 to June 2026, Malaysian and Singaporean ministers said in a joint statement on Monday, according to CNA and The Business Times.

Mon Nov 2diplomacy

Japan urges US to enforce troop discipline after another Marine is arrested in Okinawa

Japan asked the United States on Monday to strictly enforce discipline among its troops after a US Marine was arrested in Okinawa on suspicion of drink-driving during a curfew, Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi and Chief Cabinet Secretary Minoru Kihara said, according to CNA and Kyodo News.

Sun Nov 1diplomacy

Taiwan says China's coast guard is harassing shipping off its east coast

Taiwan's Coast Guard said China's latest coast guard patrol off the island's east coast amounts to harassment of shipping and an attempt to exert a fictional jurisdiction, and it sent its own ships to monitor.

Sat Oct 31diplomacy

US raises China's 'coercive behavior' in Yellow Sea at talks with Japan and South Korea

Secretary of State Marco Rubio raised China's conduct in the Yellow Sea at a trilateral meeting with the Japanese and South Korean foreign ministers in Atlanta, the first time the State Department has named that sea in its readouts of such meetings, SBS reported.

Sat Oct 31policy

Singapore plans more than 6,000 new homes in Toa Payoh West

Singapore's Housing and Development Board (HDB) said more than 6,000 homes will be built in Toa Payoh West over the coming decade, starting with about 1,600 flats near Caldecott MRT station.

Fri Oct 30economy

Bank of Japan holds rate at 1.25%, says underlying inflation is generally at its 2% target

The Bank of Japan kept its policy rate at around 1.25% on Friday and said underlying inflation is now generally consistent with its 2% target, the first time it has made that assessment since adopting the goal in 2013, according to Kyodo News, NHK and CNBC.

Fri Oct 30markets

Seoul and Taipei stocks tumble as AI spending worries hit chipmakers

South Korea's KOSPI fell 3.48% to 5,730.74 on Friday and Taiwan's Taiex dropped 2.49% to 45,211.83, as chip stocks slid after a tech sell-off on Wall Street, according to Yonhap, Edaily and Focus Taiwan.
